sources.entry: rich - Python library for rich text and beautiful formatting in the terminal. Also provides a great RichHandler log handler.

summary.one_liner: Rich is a Python library for adding color, styling, tables, progress bars, markdown, syntax highlighting and tracebacks to terminal output.
summary.what_it_does: Rich provides a Console object with a print method similar to the builtin print, which word-wraps text to terminal width and supports inline bbcode-like markup for color and style. It includes a rich print function, a pretty-printing REPL hook, and an inspect function that reports on any Python object. Built-in renderables include log output with timestamps and file/line info, a logging handler, emoji shortcodes, flexible unicode-bordered tables that resize to terminal width, flicker-free progress bars, spinner status messages, guide-line trees, column layouts, markdown rendering, and pygments-based syntax highlighting. It can also install itself as the default traceback handler for prettier exception output.
use_cases: add colors and styling to Python command-line output
show progress bars for long-running tasks
render markdown or syntax-highlighted code in a terminal
format Python logging output with colors
how_to_run: from rich.console import Console; console = Console(); console.print("Hello, [bold magenta]World[/bold magenta]!")
notable: Console object with print and log methods and bbcode-like markup for inline styling
Tables, progress bars, trees, markdown and syntax highlighting out of the box
Works in Jupyter notebooks with no extra configuration
Companion projects Rich CLI and Textual are mentioned in the README
caveats: Classic Windows terminal is limited to 16 colors; true color and emoji need the new Windows Terminal
